newsitem.title: USA: Paper industry partner sought for Bronx project.
newsitem.headline: Paper industry partner sought for Bronx project.

text.p: Bronx Community Paper Co is seeking an industry partner for a proposed $450 million waste paper recycling plant in the Harlem River Yard in the Mott Haven/Port Morris section of the South Bronx area of New York City, according to John Melia, a spokesman for Empire State Development Corp.
Early this month, he noted, Bronx Community Paper was issued a state permit allowing construction of a state-of-the art waste paper recycling facility on 30 acres next to the Triborough Bridge.
Now it needs a capital partner to proceed with the plant, expected to employ 600 and produce 829 tons per day of quality newsprint from waste newspaper and magazines, Melia told Reuters Friday.
He said it is talking to paper producers and consumers, including New York Times Co, that might provide the capital of a bankable purchase order.

Bronx Community Paper is a venture between the Natural Resources Defense Council, a national environmental group and the Banana Kelly Community Improvement Association, a local community development corporation.

Allen Hershkowitz, co-director of Bronx Community Paper and a staff scientist at NRDC, said: "We are delighted that the State is issuing the final discretionary permit for what will be the largest industrial project to be built in New York City since World War II."

The State Department of Environmental Conservation on August 1 issued Bronx Community Paper Company an air permit, or certificate to operate, certifying the proposed facility's air emissions will meet state and U.S. clean air requirements.

DEC Commissioner John P. Cahill said the "Bronx Community Paper facility will recycle tons of waste paper annually and turn it into high-quality newsprint, preserving precious landfill space and natural resources."

The facility is proposed for a 30 acre site located in the 96 acre Harlem River Yard owned by the New York State Department of Transportation. The site has been unused for more than 25 years, according to a DEC statement.
Bronx Community Paper plans to be the only combination wastepaper sorting, deinking and newspaper manufacturing facility in the United States that uses 100 percent post- consumer waste paper.
